chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Habib al-Khath'ami who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:'

'Verily we sin and we do wrong, then we turn back penitently to Allah.' Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id said, 'There is no difference of opinion among our scholars that they (peace be upon them) are infallible from every ugliness absolutely, and that they (peace be upon them) consider abandoning what is recommended as a sin and a misdeed in relation to their perfection (peace be upon them).'
ai.seo_question: Do the Imams sin if they are infallible?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Shia scholarly consensus that the Imams' infallibility (*ismah*) protects them from major sins and error in conveying revelation, yet they voluntarily commit minor sins or omit recommended acts (*mandub*) to demonstrate humility and the virtue of repentance. By regarding the omission of a recommended act as a 'sin' relative to their exalted status, they model the ideal believer's relationship with Allah, reinforcing the concept that *ismah* is a higher degree of perfection rather than mere absence of fault. This practice underscores the practical implication that repentance is not just for the forgiven but a continuous state of the perfected.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 12.Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ḥabīb al-Khathʿamī who said, “I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh say, ‘

Verily we sin and we forget, then we turn back penitently to Allah.’” Al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿīd said, “There is no difference of opinion among our scholars that they (the Imams) are infallible and free of every type of ugliness [in their actions]. They (a) refer to the abandoning of what is recommended as a sin and a misdeed in relation to their own perfection [and that is why they repent].”
